summary: ACCEPT at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX, with a correction recorded first. My v42 ACCEPT was wrong and Codex's v42 REJECT was right on both counts. v42 left builderSignature with no wire encoding at all — a JSON record cannot carry raw bytes — and left digest case unpinned outside the public key; it also failed to extend the reserved vectors to the refusal branches it had just introduced. At v42 I ran an operand trace specifically to avoid repeating my v41 miss and recorded the signature as carried, which established presence and never asked about encoding. That is the third consecutive generation in which the other reviewer found something I did not, and although the severity has narrowed from blocker to SHOULD-FIX the direction has not changed; the habit is that I check at the level I last learned and do not descend unprompted. This generation repairs both items. A GOVERNING hexEncodingRule pins every digest in the path to exactly 64 lowercase hex and refuses uppercase, mixed case, missing leading zeros and 0x prefixes; builderPublicKey is 64 hex and builderSignature is 128 hex, decoding is strict on alphabet and length, and verification is stated to consume the decoded 32 and 64 bytes. The per-field clauses agree with the governing rule rather than merely coexisting, and the rule reaches fields Codex did not name. The G22 vectors are enumerated in the normative object and marked required rather than optional, covering zero-zero acceptance, every marker malformation on both sides, all three correct header mappings, all six ordered cross-kind mismatches which I counted individually, the signed-versus-later key mismatch, cross-event composition, both case-violation classes, both signature encoding failures and the canonical round trip. Everything from prior generations survives intact: marker cardinality, actualHeaderKind equality, the closed forms carrying key, signature and root digest, the corroboration pipeline gated to the present branch, and the capability conditioned by an iff on verification. Structure is clean — 67 of 67 pins, 23 changed paths with zero off-roster, a pure-append reviewGuidance, a byte-exact register row, reproducing remeasurement pins, 40 of 40 D-096 refusals, one structural-proof standing and no stale live references. The residual is trust, named rather than hidden: the rooted builder can attest falsely, and the closure signer both allowlists that root and carries its key, so the two roles are separated by policy and not by mechanism. Given the correction above, this ACCEPT should be weighed alongside the other reviewer's verdict rather than relied on alone.
